title: What does the 6 in 6₁ count?
hook: Knot tables give every knot a number. Is it something you can count in the picture?

knows: a knot is a closed loop of rope, and a drawing shows which strand is on top at each crossing
doesNotKnow: that the first number in a knot's table name, such as 6 in 6₁, is the fewest crossings any drawing of that knot can have, so a drawing can show more crossings than its name says; the second number is only its place in the table

misconception: The number in a knot's name counts something you can see in its drawing, such as the crossings or the loops.
objective: The learner can explain that a knot's name number is the fewest crossings any drawing of it can have, using a drawing that shows more crossings than its name.
keyState: A switched drawing whose crossings drawn differ from its name's first number (milestone 'switched', recorded as {chip, drawn, name}).

claims.text: The first number in a knot's table name is its crossing number: the fewest crossings any drawing of that knot can have ('The first number in a name is the fewest crossings any drawing of that knot can have'; recall answer 'Some drawing of it has 5 crossings, and none has fewer').
claims.source: Rolfsen, Knots and Links (1976), Appendix C knot table convention (fact-checker to confirm wording); research note company/research/notes/2026-10-13-teachable-knot-theory.md §2.5. Brief claim 1 (company/domains/briefs/math.discrete.md, Knots batch 1 #1). Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: W-1589 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): VERIFIED against Demo.tsx at 5b5341c6 (reveal, predict key, recall key) and opened secondary sources: PNAS 2022 (PMC8740703) "label X_i indicates a knot ... that can be drawn on the page with no fewer than X crossings"; PMC7015418 "the least number of crossings in any regular diagram". Rolfsen's book itself not opened (AMS host blocked; Crossref 10.1090/chel/346 confirms the book and its table chapter). Basis: company/reviews/draw-a-table-knot/2026-10-16-fact-check.md, c1.

claims.text: The kit's 6₁ drawing has 6 crossings and its 5₂ drawing has 5 ('This drawing of 6₁ has 6 crossings'; stage readout 'Crossings drawn: 6 · Name: 6₁' and '5 · 5₂').
claims.source: crossingCount(knot('6_1').pd) = 6 and crossingCount(knot('5_2').pd) = 5 on src/kit/knots; identify returns 6_1 and 5_2. Brief check K1 and K6 (node company/domains/briefs/checks/knots-check.mjs). Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: W-1589 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): VERIFIED: own Python on the kit PD codes: 6 and 5 crossings, alternating Gauss words, no nugatory crossing, own Kauffman-bracket Jones spans 6 and 5 matching published 6_1 and 5_2 (up to mirror). Geometry of the drawn picture (stored layout, gap 0): 6 and 5 crossing centres, 12 and 10 edges, 0 extra crossings in the base and every switched state. Basis: company/reviews/draw-a-table-knot/2026-10-16-fact-check.md, c2.

claims.text: 4₁ cannot be drawn with fewer than 4 crossings, and 3₁ with fewer than 3 ('4₁ can be drawn with 4 and never with fewer'; '3₁ can be drawn with 3 and never with fewer').
claims.source: Derivation: the kit's 4_1 and 3_1 drawings are reduced and alternating (simplify status 'minimal', brief check K8; K14 for the switched states). Citation: Tait's first conjecture (a reduced alternating diagram has the fewest crossings), proved 1987 by Kauffman, Murasugi and Thistlethwaite; research note §2.5 (high; full text unchecked). Brief claim 3. Cut first if held (design note cut order). Reveal sentence 'So the first number in a name is not what one drawing shows' cut W-1586 for the word budget; it carried no claim of its own (its content is c1's first clause and c5's switch result). Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: W-1589 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): VERIFIED: own Jones spans 4 (4_1) and 3 (3_1) and the Kauffman-Murasugi-Thistlethwaite bound span V <= crossings of any diagram give the lower bounds; the kit drawings with 4 and 3 crossings give the upper bounds. The three 1987 Topology papers confirmed on Crossref (26:395-407, 26:187-194, 26:297-309); full texts not opened (Elsevier blocked); restated and applied in Nat Commun 2019 (PMC6384881). Basis: company/reviews/draw-a-table-knot/2026-10-16-fact-check.md, c3.

claims.text: The second number in a table name is only the knot's place in the table's list among knots with that crossing number ('The second number is only its place in the table').
claims.source: Rolfsen, Knots and Links (1976), Appendix C table convention (fact-checker to confirm). Brief claim 4. Wording shortened W-1586 (text changed, reset to unverified). Cut second if held (design note cut order). Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: W-1589 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): VERIFIED: PNAS 2022 (PMC8740703) "i is an arbitrary index to distinguish different knots ... with minimal crossing number X"; Angew Chem 2017 (PMC5582600) "Y is an index that distinguishes the knot from others with the same number of crossings". Rolfsen not opened. Basis: company/reviews/draw-a-table-knot/2026-10-16-fact-check.md, c4.

claims.text: In the kit's 6₁ drawing, switching any one crossing gives 4₁ (4 of 6) or a plain loop 0₁ (2 of 6); in its 5₂ drawing, a trefoil 3₁ (3 of 5, the mirror image, listed under 3₁) or a plain loop (2 of 5); the drawing keeps 6 (or 5) crossings ('Your switch made a new knot. Your 6₁ still had 6 crossings drawn, but its name became 4₁'; stage readout and Seen line).
claims.source: crossingChange, identify and crossingCount on src/kit/knots; brief check K14 (node company/domains/briefs/checks/knots-check.mjs): 6_1 4_1 x4, 0_1 x2; 5_2 3_1* x3, 0_1 x2; pictures keep 6/12 and 5/10 crossings/edges. Builder's node re-run 2026-10-16: 6_1 switches 0,2,3,5 -> 4_1, 1,4 -> 0_1; 5_2 switches 0,2,4 -> 3_1 (mirror), 1,3 -> 0_1. The stage reads identify()[0].name; the mirror flag is not shown. Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: cm-math-discrete, 2026-10-17: claim text changed for lesson v2: the reveal now names the switched knot ('Your 6₁ still had 6 crossings drawn', was 'Yours still had'), from finding 4 of company/reviews/draw-a-table-knot/2026-10-16-learner-knows-drawings-not-names.md; the switch results are unchanged; reset to unverified for a fact-checker who did not write the wording. Previous: W-1591 re-verify (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim or draft the new wording): VERIFIED at 5c5c719e. 'Your switch made a new knot.' is true in every state that can reach the reveal: the reveal needs milestone 'switched', tap() records the switch before reach(), so seen is never null there (the 6_1 to 4_1 fallback is unreachable), and only one crossing is ever switched (crossingChange(base, i) from the base drawing). Own no-kit check (PD codes dumped from the kit, then own arcs, colouring-matrix determinant and Kauffman bracket): 6_1 det 9; its switches 0,2,3,5 det 5 and Jones span 4 (4_1), 1,4 det 1 and span 0 (unknot). 5_2 det 7; switches 0,2,4 det 3 span 3 (3_1), 1,3 det 1 span 0. Determinant is a knot invariant, so all 11 single switches give a knot different from the one switched; names follow from span = crossing number for these (alternating, at most 6 crossings). Crossing counts stay 6 and 5. Record: company/reviews/draw-a-table-knot/2026-10-16-fact-check.md, W-1591 section. Before: W-1591 (demo-builder, 2026-10-16): reveal first sentence changed to the fact-checker's exact fix "Your switch made a new knot." (6 words for 6) and the quote above updated; reset to unverified for a fact-checker who did not draft the wording. Previous: W-1589 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): DISPUTED, rendered text only (the switch results are right): the reveal opens "A switch makes a new knot.", a general statement that is false for a nugatory crossing (switching a kink leaves the knot unchanged) and, for other crossings, is the open cosmetic crossing conjecture (Boninger 2023, Proc AMS Ser B, 10.1090/bproc/184). The recall's own 9-crossing 5_2 drawing must have such extra crossings. Exact fix (Demo.tsx Reveal, same 6 words): "Your switch made a new knot." and the claim text quote updated to match. Results re-derived: 6_1 switches 0,2,3,5 -> 4_1, 1,4 -> 0_1; 5_2 switches 0,2,4 -> 3_1 (mirror of the kit entry), 1,3 -> 0_1; 6 and 5 crossings kept. Basis: company/reviews/draw-a-table-knot/2026-10-16-fact-check.md, c5.

claims.text: A plain loop (0₁) can be drawn with no crossings ('its name became 0₁, a plain loop'; 'a plain loop can be drawn with none'; stage 'Name: 0₁, plain loop').
claims.source: The unknot is the round circle, crossing number 0; table entry 0_1 in src/kit/knots (KNOTS['0_1'].c = 0) and Rolfsen's table convention. simplify status 'unknot' for the 0_1 switches (K14). Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: W-1589 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, did not write this claim): VERIFIED: convention; Angew Chem 2017 (PMC5582600) "A trivial knot has no crossings ... the unknot, denoted 0_1". The 0_1 switch states: own Jones = 1 on a diagram of at most 6 crossings, so the knot is the unknot (every nontrivial knot up to 7 crossings is alternating with span = crossing number >= 3). Basis: company/reviews/draw-a-table-knot/2026-10-16-fact-check.md, c6.

claims.text: Knot tables name each knot with a number, and the table draws each knot with the fewest crossings, so the kit's 6₁ drawing (and 5₂ drawing) has exactly 6 (and 5) ('Knot tables name each knot with a number, like 6₁'; 'The table draws each knot with that fewest, so 6₁ had exactly 6').
claims.source: Rolfsen, Knots and Links (1976), Appendix C: tabulated diagrams are minimal (fact-checker to confirm). Kit: the 6_1 and 5_2 drawings are reduced alternating, simplify status 'minimal', drawn = c (brief checks K1, K6). Builder-written; unverified.

recall.question: A drawing of a knot shows 9 crossings. Its table name is 5₂. What follows?
options: Some drawing of it has 5 crossings, and none has fewer
The name is wrong; it should start with 9
Every drawing of it has 9 crossings
recall.why: The first number in a table name is the fewest crossings any drawing of the knot can have. A drawing can show more; the table's own drawing shows the fewest.
